clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old pregnant woman presented with right shoulder pain, persistent dyspnea since first pregnancy, and new cough and hemoptysis in the second pregnancy. Chest X-ray revealed a tumor mass in the right lung near the scapula. Clinical exam showed local swelling and attenuated breath sounds. MRI showed multiple suspicious lesions in the lung, mediastinum, scapula, and vertebral osteolytic lesion. Fine-needle biopsy of the lung tumor and open biopsy of the scapula lesion were performed after cesarean section. Immunohistochemistry diagnosed NUT midline carcinoma. FISH analysis did not detect typical NUT gene rearrangements due to a cryptic translocation. PET-CT performed after delivery showed multiple metastases including both breasts.
